acceptance.given: Consumer route closure is validated against the current Toolchain call surface and frozen required Consumer Manifest, with each required route check represented by an executable selector and invocation.

oracle.expected: A fresh validation run proves every required Consumer route check is executable on every success path and binds each route-check identity, invocation command, and success-path observation.
forbidden: A required Consumer route check is bypassed or unreachable on a successful path.
Success is reported while required route checks cannot execute.
oracle.observable: Structured route-closure evidence records every required Consumer route check as reachable, with no missing, skipped, or unreachable checks.

acceptance.then: The reachability proof is persisted with replay/Consumer evidence for independent acceptance inspection.
acceptance.when: Run Consumer-closure validation after bidirectionally reconciling the frozen manifest with repository callers and exercising each required route through its real invocation path.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the S7 route-closure test with a fixture marking one required route unreachable on an otherwise successful path; validation must reject success.
Execute the S7 route-closure test with one required Consumer route omitted from the reconciled manifest/call surface; validation must fail closed.

affected_subjects: Consumer manifest and repository call-surface reconciliation
slice_hint.behavior_change: Require observed execution and reachability evidence for every required Consumer route check before reporting success; reject omitted, skipped, or unreachable checks while preserving bidirectional manifest/call-surface reconciliation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay and Consumer-manifest interfaces; rollback restores prior route-closure verdict and diagnostic bindings without weakening required-check execution.

slice_hint.state_transition: Consumer closure transitions from success without an independent success-path reachability proof to success only after every required route check has an executable observed invocation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Success is terminal only when the reconciled required Consumer Manifest has a real invocation and reachable success-path observation for every route check; missing, unreachable, skipped, or omitted checks yield an unsuccessful deterministic verdict.

acceptance.given: A Matrix Case execution has independently bound Stable and Candidate inputs, frozen expected output and expectation identities, and real two-sided observations available to the aggregate evaluator.

oracle.expected: When either the expected output bytes or the expectation record is tampered after binding, aggregate evaluation deterministically returns an unsuccessful invalidation result and records the forged-artifact diagnostic.
forbidden: Forged expected output is accepted as case evidence.
A forged expectation allows the aggregate to succeed.
The aggregate reports success using copied or stale expectation material.
oracle.observable: The runtime aggregate receipt shows the tampered expected-output or expectation identity mismatch, the affected Matrix Case is invalid, and the aggregate terminal verdict is unsuccessful.

acceptance.then: Execute the Matrix aggregate with one isolated mutation to a bound expected output or expectation while holding all other case inputs and subject executions constant; verify the real evaluator rejects the case and aggregate.
acceptance.when: The Matrix aggregate evaluator verifies frozen expectations and expected outputs against the identities bound for the current run.

affected_subjects: Matrix aggregate expectation verification and terminal verdict calculation
slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or repair runtime verification so any forged expected output or expectation identity causes the affected Matrix Case and its aggregate to become unsuccessful; preserve independent Stable/Candidate execution and deterministic diagnostic classification.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing Matrix receipt and terminal-category compatibility; on rollback the evaluator must continue rejecting forged expectation identities without weakening two-sided execution or evidence binding.

slice_hint.state_transition: Given a bound Matrix aggregate, mutate exactly one expected output or expectation artifact, run the real aggregate evaluator, and transition the case and aggregate to an unsuccessful forged-evidence result with attributable mismatch evidence.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The aggregate terminal result is unsuccessful whenever any expected output or expectation identity differs from the bound value; no forged artifact can yield aggregate success.

acceptance.given: Toolchain aggregate evaluation is determining a Matrix run with one or more required Matrix Case inputs or subject executions missing.

oracle.expected: The aggregate result is reported as failed whenever required execution coverage is incomplete.
forbidden: The aggregate passes despite a missing required execution.
A missing Matrix Case execution is ignored by aggregate evaluation.
oracle.observable: The aggregate result and required Matrix Case execution-coverage evaluation are inspected after the Matrix run is evaluated.

acceptance.then: Aggregate success is possible only with complete required execution coverage.
acceptance.when: Required Matrix Case execution coverage is assessed by the Toolchain aggregate evaluator.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run aggregate evaluation with a required Matrix Case input or subject execution omitted and require the aggregate evaluation to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make Toolchain matrix aggregate evaluation fail whenever required Matrix Case input or either required subject execution is absent.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema or persisted-state migration; rollback restores prior aggregate evaluation behavior only.

slice_hint.state_transition: Incomplete required Matrix Case execution coverage -> failed aggregate result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The aggregate evaluator reports success only after all required Matrix Case inputs and subject executions are present.

acceptance.given: An applicable Consumer has a bound Prior Route identity and baseline verdict and diagnostic category, plus a current Candidate Route.

oracle.expected: Real Consumer call receipts show enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable; after the sequence the observed Prior Route identity, verdict, and diagnostic category equal the captured baseline.
forbidden: Prior Route identity is not restored.
The verdict baseline is not restored.
The diagnostic baseline is not restored.
Configuration-only switching is treated as behavioral rollback.
oracle.observable: The Consumer-transition result contains real-call observations for all four transitions and a final comparison with the captured Prior Route baseline.

acceptance.then: The Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline are restored after the complete transition sequence.
acceptance.when: The applicable Consumer executes enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through its real call surface.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use a controlled Consumer transition whose rollback receipt has a changed Prior Route identity, verdict, or diagnostic category and observe the behavior test fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Execute enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through each applicable real Consumer call surface and compare the final Prior Route identity, verdict, and diagnostic baseline with the captured baseline.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Route-transition evidence remains non-authorizing and rollback restores the Prior Route baseline without schema migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: Bound Prior Route baseline -> Candidate enabled -> Prior Route invoked for disable and rollback -> Candidate re-enabled with Prior Route baseline restored.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every applicable Consumer has real-call receipts for all four transitions, and the final observed Prior Route identity, verdict, and diagnostic category equal its captured baseline.
